title: The Umbrella Club
question: What if a storm knocks over a stand?
phrase: A little now, so a big loss isn't all mine.

steps.say: Did anyone say “what do they get if I say yes?” this week?
Last night a storm knocked over the baker's stand. Fixing it costs 8 coins.

steps.turn: Can the baker fix the stand alone?

options.label: Yes
options.hint: The baker has 3 coins. Fixing costs 8.

steps.turn: How many coins are in the pot?

options.hint: Four stands, 2 coins each. Count by twos.
Four stands, 2 coins each. Count by twos.

steps.say: Round 1. Four stands start a club. Each puts 2 coins in a pot.

steps.turn: Is 8 enough to fix one stand?

options.label: Not enough
options.hint: Fixing a stand costs 8. The pot has 8.

steps.say: Round 2. The club pays to fix whichever stand a storm hits.

steps.turn: Join the umbrella club for 2 coins?
steps.justForYou: This is the idea under insurance: a small cost now against a big loss later. Either choice teaches it.
steps.say: Round 3. This one is real. Storm clouds are coming.
The storm hit your stand! The club paid to fix it.
The storm hit your stand. Fixing it cost you 8 coins.
The storm missed you. Your 2 coins helped fix a neighbor's stand.
The storm missed you this time. You kept your coins.

options.label: The club is a waste if no storm hits me
options.hint: Where did the club's coins go when a storm hit a neighbor?

options.label: Everyone pays a little, so nobody loses a lot

steps.say: That is what a club is for. A little now, so a big loss isn't all mine.

steps.turn: Say it together: a little now, so a big loss isn't all mine.
How many cups will you make?
steps.say: Now run your stand for a day. Use what you know.

steps.turn: People are coming! Tap to serve each one.

steps.say: You sold {earned} cups. {left} were left over.
Find something that protects us. A little now, so a big loss isn't all mine.
